cells.tense: Right now the work is in your hands and what you tended has actually come in.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you finished this week, plainly, and let the sentence end there.
cells.core:
You built something and it's carrying weight now. Not a plan, not a maybe — a thing you worked at until it could stand without you, and you kept the direction through the parts that dragged. That's drive when it's working: not pushing anymore, but knowing the aim got you somewhere real, and being able to stand next to it without reaching for the next rung.

The easy slip comes right after. When a thing is done, the engine wants somewhere new to point, and the fruit gets walked past before it's eaten. The momentum already proved itself getting here. Nothing you do in the next week has to earn that, and nothing you leave sitting for a day gets lost.
cells.sheetLine: The work came in. Let yourself be in the room with it.
cells.verb: tending until what you made comes in
cells.place: a body with momentum aimed somewhere it chose

cells.tense: You're pushing toward the next thing before this one has even been brought in.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you're proudest of and leave it alone for a week. Don't improve it.
cells.core:
Your drive has run ahead of what's actually here. Somewhere past the work that exists is a version where everything finally adds up, and you're bracing for it — planting more, pushing harder, heading off a shortfall that hasn't shown up. The thing you already grew is getting walked past on the way to the one that isn't real yet, and the walking is the part that costs you.

What you're calling foresight is restlessness wearing its coat. The care that built this didn't exhaust you, and it doesn't have to now. Bringing what grew together with what you know, instead of another push, is the move — the garden is already full, and full gardens don't need another row planted in the dark.

cells.tense: The work got built and finished, but you're standing at the edge of it without going in.
cells.ask: Name the one direction you'd head next if you already knew it would work. Say it out loud, once.
cells.core:
The engine is running but there's nothing under it. The thing got made, the work got done, and deciding what any of it was for started costing more than doing it — so the drive went into holding, and here you sit, at the edge of something finished, not walking into it, not walking away from it either.

It isn't effort that's missing. It's a direction to spend it on. Pick the one you'd head toward if the outcome were guaranteed, and let that pull instead of pushing yourself at nothing. What shines comes from what got developed, and a direction chosen is already half of that.
cells.sheetLine: The next direction is the thing that's missing, not the effort.

cells.tense: You've already been steering toward this and you talk about it like it happened on its own.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you're the one who kept this going. Then say what you want next.
cells.core:
There's something you're moving toward and you've been calling it circumstances. The careful choices, the small steady work, the direction you held when it got hard — none of that gets credited to you in your own accounting. It reads as luck, or timing, or the market, or someone else's push, and the account keeps coming out empty.

But the momentum is yours. You aimed it, and you kept aiming it. What would change is not more commitment into the same direction — it's naming who's been at the wheel the whole time. Once that's on your side of the ledger, the next choice gets easier, because you're the one making it.
cells.sheetLine: You've been steering this. Say so, and the wheel stops feeling stuck.

attempts.check: The record says the mechanism is GROWTH feeding the balance, but I've written Dedication's ask as a deed of commitment rather than a rest in completion; a reader could say the medicine points to surrender flowing from a finished thing, not to a new attempt. The ask survives being wrong because telling one person what you're proud of is useful whether or not my read of Drive is exact. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that makes the tending sound like a verdict rather than a stake.
